answer: Price identity as recurring, non-hedgeable risk, not a fee. Each epoch the saffron beacon fixes one unselectable direction every identity must bond on; losers lose principal. All N shells sit on that side, so N multiplies exposure instead of diversifying it; the pool settles, blocking internal offsets. Each bond is an unspent, serial-numbered stake unit: one coin cannot back two names, so the attacker locks N units of real capital per epoch. A shell cannot wander to a fresh inlet to reset losses; age is tracked per inlet and switching raises the bond. Fees are resalable; losses recur.
